title: App Service backups, networking and deployment slots
learningObjective: Configure backup and restore, inbound and outbound networking (access restrictions, private endpoints, VNet integration), and deployment slots with safe swaps.
foundation: Backups keep copies of your app's content and configuration so you can restore after a mistake.
Networking settings control who can reach your app (inbound) and what your app can reach (outbound), such as a database on a private network.
Deployment slots are extra copies of your app, such as 'staging'. You deploy there, test it, then swap it into production with no downtime.
engineer: Backups: automatic backups (platform-managed, hourly, kept 30 days) are available in Basic and higher. Automatic backups need no storage account and have a 30 GB limit. Custom backups are also available from Basic (on Basic, only the production slot can be backed up): they go to your storage account on demand or on a schedule (at most every 2 hours), have a 10 GB limit including any linked database, and keep backups 0–30 days or indefinitely. Automatic backups never include databases; support for linked databases in custom backups ends on 31 March 2028, so plan database-native backups. Restore to the same app, another app or a slot.

Inbound networking: access restrictions (priority-ordered allow/deny rules by IP range, service tag or VNet subnet with service endpoint; separate rules for the SCM/Kudu site); private endpoints (Basic and higher) give the app a private IP and can be combined with disabling public network access, plus privatelink.azurewebsites.net private DNS.

Outbound networking: regional VNet integration (Basic and higher) lets the app call resources in or through a VNet (private endpoints, VMs, on-premises over gateways) from a dedicated, delegated integration subnet; enable route-all (vnetRouteAllEnabled) to send all outbound traffic through the VNet for NSGs, UDRs and NAT gateway. Hybrid connections reach specific host:port endpoints on-premises.

Deployment slots (Standard: 5, Premium/Isolated: 20): each slot has its own hostname and can be deployed independently. Swap exchanges content and non-sticky settings; settings marked 'Deployment slot setting' stay with the slot. Some settings never swap: custom domains, TLS bindings, scale settings, IP restrictions, Always On, VNet integration, managed identities, WebJobs schedulers and diagnostic settings.

Swap safety: the target slot's settings are applied to the source instances, which are warmed up (applicationInitialization) before routing switches. Swap with preview (multi-phase) pauses so you can validate. Auto swap is available for Windows apps. Testing in production routes a percentage of traffic to a slot. Rollback = swap again.

example.title: Zero-downtime releases
body: Every release deploys to the staging slot, which has its own sticky connection string to a staging database. A smoke test runs against app-contoso-staging.azurewebsites.net, then a swap with preview promotes it.
The production app is reachable only through a private endpoint from Front Door, calls Azure SQL through VNet integration, and has daily custom backups to a storage account.

prerequisites: Basic tier for backups (Standard for deployment slots)
Integration subnet (delegated to Microsoft.Web/serverFarms) for VNet integration
permissions: Storage Blob Data Contributor or SAS for backup storage
limits: Custom backup limit 10 GB including databases
portal: Web app > Backups: configure custom backups (storage container, schedule, databases); restore.
Web app > Networking: Access restriction, Private endpoints, VNet integration, Hybrid connections.
Web app > Deployment slots > Add slot; Swap (with preview); Traffic %.
Configuration: tick 'Deployment slot setting' on app settings that must stay with a slot.
configuration.cli:
az webapp config backup create -g rg-web --webapp-name app-contoso --backup-name manual1 --container-url "<container-SAS-URL>"
az webapp config backup update -g rg-web --webapp-name app-contoso --container-url "<container-SAS-URL>" --frequency 1d --retain-one true --retention 30
az webapp config access-restriction add -g rg-web -n app-contoso --rule-name office --action Allow --ip-address 203.0.113.0/24 --priority 100
az webapp vnet-integration add -g rg-web -n app-contoso --vnet vnet-app --subnet snet-integration
az resource update -g rg-web -n app-contoso --resource-type Microsoft.Web/sites --set properties.vnetRouteAllEnabled=true
az webapp deployment slot create -g rg-web -n app-contoso --slot staging
az webapp config appsettings set -g rg-web -n app-contoso --slot staging --slot-settings ConnectionStrings__Db="<staging-db>"
az webapp traffic-routing set -g rg-web -n app-contoso --distribution staging=10
az webapp deployment slot swap -g rg-web -n app-contoso --slot staging --target-slot production
configuration.powershell:
New-AzWebAppBackup -ResourceGroupName rg-web -Name app-contoso -StorageAccountUrl '<container-SAS-URL>'
New-AzWebAppSlot -ResourceGroupName rg-web -Name app-contoso -Slot staging
Switch-AzWebAppSlot -ResourceGroupName rg-web -Name app-contoso -SourceSlotName staging -DestinationSlotName production
Add-AzWebAppAccessRestrictionRule -ResourceGroupName rg-web -WebAppName app-contoso -Name office -Priority 100 -Action Allow -IpAddress 203.0.113.0/24

lab.objective: Configure backups and private networking, and perform a safe slot swap.
steps: Deployment slots: run with defaults, then apply 'Staging DB string not sticky' and 'Basic tier'.
Backup and networking: run with defaults, then apply 'Free tier backup' and 'No VNet integration'.
expected: Non-sticky connection strings swap into production
Private DB access needs VNet integration

validation.text: Configured private inbound and outbound networking

failureScenarios: Calling a private endpoint without VNet integration
lab.cost: None. The simulation runs entirely in the browser.

troubleshooting.symptom: After a swap, production uses the staging database.
troubleshooting.cause: Connection string not marked as a deployment slot setting.
troubleshooting.fix: Mark it sticky, swap back, then swap again.

troubleshooting.symptom: App cannot reach SQL through its private endpoint.
troubleshooting.cause: No VNet integration, or private DNS not resolving from the integration subnet.
troubleshooting.fix: Enable VNet integration and link privatelink.database.windows.net to the VNet.

troubleshooting.symptom: 403 from the office after adding access restrictions.
troubleshooting.cause: Rule priority or missing allow rule for the office range.
troubleshooting.fix: Check rules; remember the implicit deny once any allow rule exists.

troubleshooting.cause: Content plus database exceeds 10 GB or storage SAS expired.
troubleshooting.fix: Exclude files, renew SAS, or use database-native backups.

comparisons.service: Azure Front Door + private link to App Service
comparisons.difference: Global entry point with WAF in front of a privately reachable app.

misconceptions.reality: Instances are warmed before routing switches.
Sticky settings and a list of platform settings never swap.

misconceptions.myth: VNet integration makes the app private.
misconceptions.reality: It is outbound only; use private endpoints/access restrictions for inbound.

architectureDecisions: Use staging slots plus swap with preview for every production release.
Combine private endpoints (inbound) and VNet integration (outbound) for private apps.
Back up databases with their native features as well.

walkthrough.subtitle: Back up a web app, connect it privately to your network, and release new versions without downtime.
learn: Inbound: access restrictions and private endpoints
Deployment slots, swap and sticky settings

steps.label: Release day
steps.title: Friday release, Monday outage
body: Deploying straight to production means users see errors while the new version starts. And the app must reach a database that has no public access.

steps.label: Slots
steps.title: Deployment slots and swap
body: A slot is a live copy of the app with its own URL (Standard: 5 slots, Premium: 20). Deploy to staging, warm it up, then swap: production now runs v2 with no downtime. Swap back if something breaks.

callout.text: Settings marked 'Deployment slot setting' (sticky) stay with the slot; others move with the code. Make database connection strings sticky.

steps.label: Backups
steps.title: Backups
body: Basic tier and higher take automatic backups. Custom backups (with a storage account and schedule) let you choose what and how often, including linked databases. Restore to the same app, another app or a slot.

steps.label: Inbound
steps.title: Control who can reach the app
body: Access restrictions allow or deny by IP range, service tag or VNet subnet, in priority order. A private endpoint gives the app a private IP and can remove public access.

steps.label: Outbound
steps.title: Let the app reach private resources
body: VNet integration sends the app's outbound traffic into a subnet of your VNet, so it can reach private endpoints and databases. It does not make the app private for inbound users.

steps.label: Recap
steps.title: App Service operations
body: Slots for releases, backups for safety, two network directions.
recap: Slots (Standard+): deploy, warm up, swap, swap back
Sticky settings stay with the slot
Automatic backups Basic+; custom backups for control

handsOn.title: Swap a staging slot into production (one hour on Standard)
handsOn.cost: Standard S1 costs roughly US$0.10 per hour. Do this lab in one sitting and delete the resource group straight after.
before: Signed in at portal.azure.com as Owner of a subscription (a free or pay-as-you-go account works). Work in a resource group called rg-az104-lab.
If rg-az104-lab does not exist yet: search 'Resource groups' > Create > name rg-az104-lab, region UAE North (or any region near you) > Review + create > Create.
A web app (from the App Service plans lab).

steps.do: Open the app's plan > Scale up > Standard S1 > Apply.
Open the app > Deployment > Deployment slots > + Add slot. Name: staging, clone settings from the production app. Add.
steps.see: Two slots: production and staging, each with its own URL.

steps.do: Open the staging slot > Settings > Environment variables. Add VERSION = v2 and tick 'Deployment slot setting'. Add GREETING = hello-v2 without the tick. Apply.
In the production slot add VERSION = v1 (sticky) only.
Back on Deployment slots select Swap: source staging, target production. Read the 'Config changes' preview. Swap.
steps.see: The preview shows GREETING moving to production while VERSION stays in each slot.
GREETING = hello-v2 moved with the swap; VERSION is still v1 (sticky).
Inbound (access restrictions, private endpoints) and outbound (VNet integration) settings.
Automatic backups available at this tier, and the option to configure custom backups.

check: You swapped slots and saw sticky settings stay behind.
cleanup: Delete the resource group now: Standard plans are billed by the hour.
When you finish for the day: Resource groups > rg-az104-lab > Delete resource group > type the name > Delete. This removes everything inside it.
